Bounced across mountains, it reaches safety unharmed. It fearlessly crosses thistles, carries companions and Hank, and later discusses beauty, insisting loveliness includes inward as well as outward qualities.

l: Land of Oz, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Land of Oz is a wonderful, astonishing fairyland ruled by Princess Ozma, its girl and supreme ruler. It is divided into four great countries, Munchkin, Quadling, Gillikin, and Winkie, with the Emerald City at their meeting place; the Winkie Country occupies a quarter of its territory. Oz is large, with remote cracks, corners, regions, and queer people, some of whom may never visit the Emerald City. Its inhabitants generally live under Ozma’s rule and are considered good and considerate, though unexplored regions may contain wicked creatures. No one can die or be killed there, and it has no soldiers or policemen apart from one soldier. Animals, birds, and fishes can speak the human language. The action begins with Ozma’s rule over this deathless land. After Glinda’s magical supplies are stolen and Ozma disappears, inhabitants search through Oz’s countries while the Wizard and others refuse to seek a new ruler. Ugu steals magic from the Emerald City, Glinda’s castle, and the Yip Country, seeks Oz’s magical possessions, and plans to master the realm. Expeditions oppose him, and the Wizard maintains that Ozma remains ruler wherever she is hidden. The whole land ends by celebrating Ozma’s safe return with cheering, decorations, feasting, and a week of festivities.

l: Munchkin Country, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Munchkin Country is one of Ozma’s four great countries in the Land of Oz, called its prettiest by the Scarecrow; Betsy Bobbin proposes visiting it with Dorothy and Trot.

l: Ozma’s royal palace, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Ozma’s royal palace is Ozma’s splendid home, with her royal suite, throne room, extensive grounds, and rooms for Dorothy, Betsy Bobbin, Trot, and the Wizard of Oz. It is central to Ozma’s friends’ search when she vanishes: they find no trace of her, remain there uneasily, and later Ugu enters through the Magic Dishpan, steals magical possessions, and captures Ozma.

l: three girls (Dorothy, Betsy Bobbin, and Trot), The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Dorothy, Betsy Bobbin, and Trot are close friends living in rooms at Ozma’s royal palace. As travelers with the Wizard and animals, they plan a journey to Munchkin Country and seek Ozma; later, they eat yellow berries and sleep together under a blanket.

l: Sawhorse, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Sawhorse is a famous, swift wooden animal and quaint, tireless steed, with a chopped-out mouth and knot eyes. Made of wood, it never sleeps, needs no food or drink, and cannot be harmed by Ugu’s magic, though it cannot harm him. It understands spoken directions for speed and direction, so it draws the Red Wagon without reins or a driver. It stays awake at the shepherd’s hut and talks with Scraps and the Woozy, then carries Button-Bright and the Wizard across thistles and to the city wall after the wagon is left behind. It later praises its own beauty and duties.

l: Red Wagon, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Red Wagon, drawn by the Sawhorse and seating four, carries Dorothy, the Wizard, Trot, Button-Bright, and supplies through the Emerald City and Winkie Country before being left behind at the Merry-Go-Round Mountains crossing.

l: the Magic Picture, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Magic Picture is Ozma’s royal treasure, a magic picture that shows what any person anywhere in the world is doing when someone wishes to see that person. It also reveals anyone approaching Ozma’s royal palace intending to conquer it. At the beginning, Dorothy, Betsy, and Trot find it missing from its usual place on the palace wall, at the same time Ozma is reported missing, so the people of the Emerald City cannot consult it to locate her. The travelers fear Ugu the Shoemaker has taken it with Ozma. Later it is found hanging in a room of Ugu’s castle, where Ugu uses it to watch the traveling party and learn of expeditions searching for him; it shows the travelers approaching in miniature. When consulted, it can show Ugu in dove form in the far Quadling Country with the golden jeweled dishpan beneath him. But when asked to show Ozma, it displays only a round black spot, revealing her concealment without showing her location.

l: Ozma’s loss, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Ozma’s loss is the sudden, unexplained disappearance of Oz’s ruler from the Emerald City. It is discovered when Dorothy finds Ozma’s royal suite empty; Ozma has not been seen since the previous evening, and her Magic Picture is missing. The loss leaves the people of the Emerald City grieved and anxious, while even Ozma’s closest friends do not know what became of her. The Wizard seeks Glinda’s help, but the Great Book of Records is also missing and the available magic cannot locate Ozma. Her friends conclude she was likely abducted by someone with magic powerful enough to prevent her escape. Glinda and several parties search Oz, while Dorothy and the Wizard continue despite uncertainty. Suspicion gradually turns toward Ugu the Shoemaker, whose ambition and possible theft of magical things link him to Ozma’s disappearance and the stolen magic of the Emerald City.

l: the search for Ozma, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The search for Ozma is a mission undertaken after Ozma cannot be found in her rooms and is missing from the palace and grounds. Dorothy, with Jellia Jamb and Scraps, searches and questions the Scarecrow, Tik-Tok, the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, Cap’n Bill, and the Wizard of Oz, but no one has seen Ozma since the previous evening. Dorothy plans an immediate search, and Glinda the Good directs several parties to ask everywhere in the Munchkin, Quadling, Gillikin, and Winkie Countries. Dorothy travels toward the Winkie Country with the Wizard, Betsy, Trot, Button-Bright, Scraps, and companions. They pursue dangerous unexplored regions despite delays, pass from the Great Orchard to Herku, and learn from Vig that Ugu the Shoemaker may have stolen Ozma. The party goes to Ugu’s castle, first rescuing Button-Bright from a hole but finding no sign of Ozma. Believing Ugu has imprisoned her, the Wizard and his followers enter the castle to rescue her; Ugu refuses to reveal her location, and Ozma is not rescued by the end of the records.

l: magic, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Magic is knowledge, practice, and learned magical trick: it can be used for good, for self-elevation, protection, deception, and coercion. Princess Ozma uses it to help her people, and no devised magic can destroy her. It can protect Ugu’s wicker castle and enable defenses such as fire, a steel wall, and an apparent army, though the Wizard can counter some of these with simple means and recognition of illusion. After magic is stolen across Oz, Ugu combines stolen objects and recipes with a year of study of his ancestors’ magic, seeking enough power to force the Land of Oz to obey him. In the end, the stolen materials are recovered, the Wizard’s powers are restored, and Ozma’s rule confines magic practice to Glinda the Good and the Wizard of Oz because others cannot be trusted not to cause harm.

l: Glinda the Good, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Glinda the Good is a powerful, good Sorceress, described as the most powerful in Oz and more magical than the Wizard of Oz. Living in her faraway castle in the Quadling Country, she serves and protects Ozma as her most valued servant, using her sorcery for the benefit of Oz’s people and able to fulfill nearly anything Ozma wishes. She travels by aerial chariot, invented a circle-of-fire trick, and possesses recipes, compounds, instruments, and the Great Book of Records. When her Book, instruments, and compounds are stolen, she is alarmed and unable to locate Ozma; she sends messengers, gathers supplies, plans replacements, and directs searches. Ugu steals the possessions from her laboratory and takes the Great Book to Wicker Castle.

l: the castle of Glinda the Good, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Glinda the Good's splendid marble-and-silver castle stands in Quadling Country, far south of the Emerald City, surrounded by serving maidens. It contains her drawing room, Room of Magic, and guarded Great Book of Records, until a thief secretly removes the book, magical instruments, and chemical compounds.

l: Quadling Country, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Quadling Country contains a far-country tree where Ugu sat; in its northeast, Ugu escapes using the golden jeweled dishpan while Scarecrow and Tin Woodman seek Ozma.

l: the Emerald City, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Emerald City is the capital where the four countries of Oz meet, surrounded by a city wall and golden gates. Ruled by and home to Ozma, it contains much magic and sorcery. Its central crisis begins when Ozma disappears and cannot be found, prompting her friends to gather and a search party to leave through the gates as the people learn the news. Later, it is among the places from which magic was stolen, and its people join the pursuit of Ugu. The story ends with Ozma’s return: the city celebrates with flags, bunting, cheers, and a grand reception, while the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman return and present Cayke’s dishpan to Ozma.

l: the Great Book of Records, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Great Book of Records is Glinda the Good’s great, magical book, immense yet thin-paged and so heavy that three men could scarcely lift it. It truthfully and exactly records important events, adventures, and all that happens throughout the known world, including Oz, the outside world, and unknown places, at the moment they occur. Kept in Glinda’s drawing room on a big gold table, chained and locked with six golden padlocks whose keys Glinda carries, it is cut free and disappears while the castle sleeps. Its loss, along with Glinda’s magic instruments, prevents Glinda and the Wizard of Oz from learning what happened to Ozma. The travelers suspect Ugu the Shoemaker; the book identifies him in the northeast corner of Quadling Country. Ugu has stolen it and examines it at the Wicker Castle, using its record of the travelers’ actions to learn that expeditions seek him, though its knowledge is dangerous to his plans.

l: the theft of Glinda's Great Book of Records, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: A mysterious theft from Glinda's castle occurs secretly while everyone sleeps: a powerful thief cuts the chains securing the heavy, locked, guarded Great Book of Records and removes it. Glinda expects the thief to be discovered and severely punished.

l: the removal of Glinda's magical supplies, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: A robbery removes all of Glinda's magical instruments and rare chemical compounds from the Room of Magic cupboard, preventing her from preparing a charm to identify the thief and prompting her to send messengers throughout Oz for replacements.

l: Cayke the Cookie Cook, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Cayke the Cookie Cook is a small Yip woman, a traveler, and a Cookie Cook of the Yips who lives in the Yip Country on a high mountain. Her greatest treasure is a diamond-studded gold Magic Dishpan, inherited from her mother and grandmothers. The dishpan enables her to make her famous, exceptionally good cookies, and without it she cannot make good cookies or be completely happy. When Ugu the Shoemaker steals the dishpan from her house, Cayke loudly reports the loss. The Yips refuse to go with her into the lower world, so she resolves to search alone; the Frogman joins her and becomes her companion. She travels down the mountain with him, persuades him to carry her across a gulf, and continues eastward through the world. She refuses to bathe in the Truth Pond because she fears being forced to tell the Frogman everything she thinks and making him dislike her. After crossing the Winkie River, she and the Frogman are taken prisoner in Bear Center, where she hopes the bears may know of the dishpan. The Bear King’s magic reveals that Ugu possesses it, so Cayke determines to confront him. She joins Dorothy’s party in pursuing Ugu, enters his castle, and sees her dishpan in his golden cage. She helps attempt to reach it through a human pyramid but declines to repeat the effort after the group falls. Ugu escapes with the dishpan, but the Magic Picture and Great Book locate it in the northeast corner of Quadling Country. Cayke is taken to the Emerald City as Ozma’s guest and receives deference, though she remains unhappy until the dishpan is restored. When it is returned, she dances, embraces Ozma, and kisses her gratefully. Her search ends, but she is not eager to leave the Emerald City.

l: the Frogman, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Frogman is a large, upright, intelligent frog who dresses and behaves like a person. Originating as a frog in a pool in the Winkie Country, he has lived for many years in the Yip Country, where he is its sole frog, adviser, and unofficial leader because the Yips have no king or queen. He lives beside an ordinary pool, wears a handsome coat and shiny purple hat, and carries a gold-headed cane. Proud of his size, culture, education, and supposed wisdom, he long claimed to be the wisest creature in the world, though he was a humbug who pretended to know more than he did. When Cayke the Cookie Cook's diamond-studded gold dishpan is stolen, the Frogman joins and helps lead the search. He first confidently promises to find it, decides that a stranger from below took it, and travels with Cayke through the Winkie Country, leaping across a gulf with her on his back. After bathing in the Truth Pond, however, he must tell the truth and admits that his superior-wisdom claims were a sham: his wisdom is no greater than Cayke's. Though he acknowledges he is a Freak rather than a Person, he remains honest, unafraid, and devoted to helping her. The search brings him through the Winkie River, Bear Center, and toward Ugu's castle, where he joins Cayke, the Bear King, Scraps, Dorothy's party, and others. His strength, courage, and jumping matter most in the final struggle. He leaps over a high steel wall in three powerful leaps and uses the Wizard's pin to make the barrier vanish. After receiving zosozo, he becomes as strong as Ugu the Shoemaker. He helps attempt to reach the stolen magic, then protects Dorothy by leaping onto Ugu's dove form and fighting it despite damage to his clothes. He assists in rescuing Ozma, receives her thanks, and afterward becomes a favorite at the Emerald City.

l: the Yips, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Yips are inhabitants of an isolated broad tableland, linked by odd paths among scattered houses and previously confined to Yip Country. They bring Cayke to the Frogman, then nine daring young Yips descend with them, clear a difficult path, and retreat at an uncrossable gulf.

l: Winkie Country, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Winkie Country is a country forming a quarter of the Land of Oz. It has settled, prosperous eastern and western regions, with rough, little-known territory and branches of the Winkie River between them. Its west reaches the Deadly Desert and includes tin mines and grain farms. During the search for news of Ozma, travelers cross the Winkie River near the vacant Scarecrow’s Tower, enter the Rolling Prairie, and later head east across part of the country toward the river. It also contains the City of Thi.

l: the Yip Country, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Yip Country is a wee, isolated country on a broad tableland in the far southwestern Winkie Country, reached only by steep, bramble-covered hills. It has houses, fields, trees, paths, the Frogman's home, and Cayke's jeweled gold Magic Dishpan. Its story begins with the first known theft, unfolds as Ugu steals the dishpan at night, and sends the Frogman and companions searching for it.

l: the Magic Dishpan, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Magic Dishpan is Cayke the Cookie Cook’s greatest treasure: a large, round beaten-gold dishpan, studded with three rows of diamonds. A family heirloom inherited through her mother and grandmothers since the beginning of time, it is cherished by Cayke and is believed to make whoever owns it a good cook. After it is stolen, Cayke’s cookies burn, become too tough, or are unusually poor. Mysteriously taken from Cayke’s house in the Yip Country on the same night Ozma disappears, the dishpan’s loss drives Cayke to leave the tableland and search the lower world with the Frogman. She suspects the Lavender Bear or bears of Bear Center, but the Bear King’s magic image and the Little Pink Bear reveal that Ugu the Shoemaker possesses it. The dishpan is also a magic instrument: it can grow large enough for a man to sit in, and someone grasping both handles can be transported anywhere within the borders of the Land of Oz. Ugu uses it to travel instantly to Quadling Country and to plunder Glinda the Good, the Wizard of Oz, and Ozma of Oz, carrying them or their possessions to the Wicker Castle. Cayke later finds it in Ugu’s golden cage but cannot retrieve it. It remains missing when the party reaches the Emerald City, where Ozma promises it will be restored; Cayke says she cannot be fully happy without it.

l: theft of the dishpan, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The theft of Cayke’s jeweled, valuable magic dishpan is the first theft in the Yip Country and occurs on the morning of Ozma’s disappearance. Cayke discovers it missing, prompting a failed proclamation and suspicion that someone entered from the world below. Cayke leaves to search with the Frogman, later joining Dorothy’s party’s search; Ugu is identified as the thief.

l: the journey to recover the dishpan, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The journey to recover the dishpan is undertaken by Cayke the Cookie Cook, the Frogman, and nine Yips toward the lower world. They descend a steep mountainside, camp in a cave, and, after the Yips retreat at a gulf, the Frogman leaps across carrying Cayke.

l: Winkies, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Winkies are people of the Winkie Country, generally prosperous and ruled by the tin Emperor Nick Chopper, subject to Ozma of Oz; some mine tin while others farm, including Wiljon and Nellary.

l: the Winkie River, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: has_branch west branch The travelers reach the west branch of the Winkie River and stay with its ferryman. He rows Cayke and the Frogman across it at sunrise, after which they continue east through a little-traveled area.

l: Tin Woodman, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Tin Woodman, Emperor of the Winkies, has a tender tin heart and punishes a ferryman for cruelty to a fox, birds, and a fish. He is assigned to Quadling Country, stays at Professor H. M. Wogglebug’s college, takes Patent Educational Pills, and carries an oilcan.

l: Wizard’s black bag of magic tools, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Wizard of Oz’s black bag of magic tools disappears before he retrieves it, leaving him without wizardry and suggesting a powerful enemy took magical possessions.

l: Ugu's theft of Oz's magical possessions, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Ugu carries out a coordinated theft of Oz’s magical possessions, including Ozma’s Magic Picture and other magical things, Glinda’s books, chemical compounds, instruments of sorcery, and the Wizard’s bag of magic tools. The theft appears meant to stop Ozma’s friends from locating or rescuing her. Ugu uses the Magic Dishpan to take the items to the Wicker Castle, where he arranges and stores them.

l: wicked enemy, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Wizard suspects that a wicked enemy abducted Ozma and stole the magical possessions. The friends believe this enemy must be powerful and must live in the Land of Oz, since the thief knew where the magical objects were kept.

l: Cowardly Lion, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: The Cowardly Lion is a talking, unusually large and intelligent animal, cowardly when facing danger but capable of courage in necessary fights. An old friend of Dorothy, he guards Ozma’s throne on state occasions and joins the search for Ozma because he is anxious for her. He leads the procession, shelters Toto at night, and travels with the Woozy. Thistles drive him back while he carries Dorothy toward a mysterious city; although afraid, he rides the Woozy and arrives safely. His fiercest asset is his roar, which frightens enemies, and he tells Toto that individual differences make them distinguished.

l: Hank the Mule, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Hank the Mule is a lean, bony, plain-looking but faithful and steady mule, a great fighter who never gets lost. Before entering the Land of Oz he lost his bray; afterward he can talk. Pricked by thistles, he retreats, then trembles across their field to safety and argues with the Woozy about beauty.

l: Toto, The Lost Princess of Oz
s: Toto is Dorothy’s little, shaggy black dog and a member of the search party. Though he can speak, he seldom says anything; he is often silent and sober, can bark, and is associated with a growl. After Dorothy leaves the Emerald City without him, Toto follows the party, hides until the shepherd’s hut, and rejoins Dorothy the next morning. Later he realizes his growl is missing, worries that its thief also stole Ozma, and finally finds it when a mouse runs from a corner.
